title: AI-Guided Design and Discovery of Silicon-Based Anode Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries
experiments_summary: The methodology consisted of three sequential stages: (1) Database Mining: Approximately 6,000 fully lithiated Si-containing compounds (Li_x Si_y X_z, where X is a metallic or metalloid element) were aggregated from multiple materials databases including the Materials Project, GNoME, OQMD, COD, SPSE, and the Marques-Halle Perovskite Dataset. Candidates were filtered for theoretical gravimetric capacities exceeding 1,500 mAh/g. For each candidate, the radius of the largest continuous Li+ migration channel in the charged-state structure was computed using geometric analysis via the CAVD package. (2) Surrogate-Assisted Structural Relaxation: Because databases report only fully lithiated (charged) structures, hypothetical discharged states were generated for each high-capacity candidate by probabilistically removing Li atoms, producing 30 distinct Li-vacancy configurations per candidate to sample different delithiation paths. These structures were then relaxed using CHGNet, a graph neural network-based machine-learning interatomic potential. After relaxation, the gravimetric capacity and Li+ migration channel radius (R_t) were recomputed for each discharged configuration. Candidates were retained only if R_t remained approximately constant between charged and discharged states, indicating stable ion transport pathways across cycling. The slope of channel radius versus state of charge was used as the key screening descriptor, with pure Si serving as a baseline (slope = 0.85 ± 0.23 Å/100%). (3) Conditional Generative Modeling: A conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) was trained on crystal graph embeddings of existing Li-Si-X anode structures and their associated properties (capacity and channel radius). The model was conditioned on target inputs including the presence of silicon, target gravimetric capacity (>1,500 mAh/g), and target channel radius R_t with minimal variation across cycling. A modified version of the conditional crystal generation model by Ye et al. was used with stronger control over elemental composition. The latent space was sampled and decoded to generate novel crystal structures, which were then evaluated using the same capacity and channel-stability screening criteria applied in Stages 1 and 2.
